items.titulo: Gemini Decisions API
items.resumen: Gemini Decisions API Google join Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with "Gemini Decision 1". This new model API is almost identical to Jev: it supports the same three types of questions (yes/no, choice, and rubric-scoring) and even reuses Jev's term "Noul" for a yes/no question. It's priced the same as the GPT-6 Luna decision model: 10 cents per million input tokens, and output is free. Jev remains the cheapest of the three, at 4.2 cents per million. Jev is text (and JSON) only. Open

items.titulo: Google Launches Gemini Decisions API With Gemini Decision 1 at $0.10/M Tokens
items.resumen: Google launched the Gemini Decisions API, powered by Gemini Decision 1. It returns calibrated probabilities for up to 1,000 yes/no, choice and rubric questions over text, images, audio, video and PDFs, at $0.10 per 1M input tokens. items.titulo: aws-emulator
items.resumen: aws-emulator Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so. It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog. It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great
